diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-2 Adjusting valve clearance
diagrams.description: Illustration showing valve clearance adjustment using Pivot Adjuster ST10640001 and feeler gauge on an OHC L-series cylinder head, with valve positions numbered 1 through 12 from front to rear.
measurements_and_specs: Pivot lock nut torque: 5.0 to 6.0 kg-m (36 to 43 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Engine oil temperature must be above 80°C (176°F). Never adjust with engine running. Rotate crankshaft four complete turns to complete all four adjustment steps.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-3 Fan belt tension
diagrams.description: Illustration demonstrating fan belt tension measurement using thumb pressure midway between alternator pulley and fan pulley.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check for cracks or damage prior to tension measurement.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-4 Cooler compressor belt tension
diagrams.description: Illustration of cooler (air conditioning) compressor belt tension check and idler pulley adjustment bolt.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust tension by turning idler pulley bolt in or out.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-5 Testing radiator cap
diagrams.description: Testing radiator pressure cap relief valve pressure using a hand pump cap tester and adapter.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Replace cap assembly if pressure is not maintained within specification.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-6 Cooling system pressure test
diagrams.description: Testing engine cooling system for leaks by applying pressure with radiator tester attached to filler neck.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Radiator cap must be removed. Inspect all hoses and joints while pressurized.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-7 Testing compression pressure
diagrams.description: Connecting compression tester gauge to spark plug port to measure cranking cylinder compression.
measurements_and_specs: Minimum: 11.5 kg/cm² (164 psi) at 300 to 400 rpm
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect cold start valve and all fuel injector connectors before cranking engine.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-8 Checking electrolyte level
diagrams.description: Visual guide for checking battery cell electrolyte levels showing Overflow, Correct, and Shortage conditions.

callouts.Shortage: Electrolyte level too low (needs distilled water)

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pour distilled water if shortage is indicated.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-9 Checking specific gravity of battery electrolyte
diagrams.description: Measuring battery electrolyte specific gravity with a glass hydrometer inserted into battery cell vent.
measurements_and_specs: Other climates: 1.26 full charge (permissible over 1.20) at 20°C (68°F)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Hold hydrometer vertical at eye level to read specific gravity scale.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-10 Adjusting ignition timing
diagrams.description: Adjusting ignition timing by loosening distributor set screw and rotating distributor housing while checking timing mark with timing light.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen set screw just enough to turn distributor by hand, align timing mark, then retighten securely.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-11 Ignition timing indicator
diagrams.description: Diagram of crankshaft pulley notch aligned with timing indicator pointer at 10 degrees BTDC.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Ensure dirt and dust are cleaned off pulley and indicator prior to reading with timing light.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-12 Checking spark plug gap
diagrams.description: Checking spark plug electrode gap using a round wire feeler gauge.
measurements_and_specs: Standard gap: 1.0 to 1.1 mm (0.039 to 0.043 in)
Canada gap: 0.7 to 0.8 mm (0.028 to 0.031 in)
Tightening torque: 1.5 to 2.0 kg-m (11 to 14 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust gap by bending ground electrode only; do not bend center electrode.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-13 Checking high tension cable
diagrams.description: Testing high tension ignition cable resistance using an ohmmeter connected between plug boot terminal and distributor cap internal terminal.
wiring_and_connections: Ohmmeter connected between spark plug terminal and distributor cap electrode
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not remove cables from cap initially. If resistance exceeds 30,000 ohms, test cable alone before replacing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-14 Adjusting idling speed
diagrams.description: Adjusting idle speed using screwdriver on idle speed adjusting screw located on throttle chamber.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Air conditioner must be OFF during idle speed inspection and adjustment.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-15 Idle mixture ratio adjustment
diagrams.description: Procedure for forcing full-load enrichment during idle CO adjustment by shorting terminals 3 and 18 of throttle valve switch connector with a jumper wire, and adjusting air flow meter bypass screw.
components: Connector of throttle valve switch harness

callouts.5: Connector of throttle valve switch harness

wiring_and_connections: Jumper wire between terminal No. 3 and No. 18 on throttle valve switch harness connector
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn bypass screw clockwise for rich mixture, counterclockwise for lean mixture.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-16 Altitude switch (California models)
diagrams.description: Location and harness disconnection point for the altitude switch on California models, situated near steering column / pedal support.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect connector when adjusting idle CO above 750 m (2,500 ft) on California models; reconnect after adjustment.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-17 Rubber plug
diagrams.description: Installing replacement rubber sealing plug into air flow meter bypass screw recess after mixture adjustment.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Install a new rubber plug (furnished as a service part) to seal air bypass screw cavity against moisture and unmetered air.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-18 Releasing pressure in fuel system
diagrams.description: Relieving residual fuel rail line pressure before filter replacement using jumper wires connected to battery and cold start valve for 2-3 seconds.
wiring_and_connections: Jumper wires from 12V battery to cold start valve harness terminals
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Prevent short circuits by keeping jumper clips separate.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-19 Fuel filter
diagrams.description: Fuel filter mounting bracket, fuel inlet/outlet hose orientation, and securing bolt location.
measurements_and_specs: Clamp torque: 0.10 to 0.15 kg-m (0.7 to 1.1 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not reuse hose clamps after loosening. Ensure clamp is positioned 1 mm from hose end.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-20 Air regulator hoses
diagrams.description: Routing of air regulator bypass hoses connecting air duct, air regulator, and intake manifold.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check for hardening, cracks, or loose clamps which introduce unmetered false air.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-21 Air cleaner filter
diagrams.description: Exploded view of the air cleaner assembly showing housing, filter element, cover, ducting, and wing nuts.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not brush or blow compressed air on viscous paper filter; replace according to maintenance schedule.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-22 Crankcase emission control system
diagrams.description: Cutaway diagram of positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) flow, showing fresh air intake pathway and blow-by gas extraction through PCV valve into intake manifold.
wiring_and_connections: Ventilator hose between crankcase baffle and PCV valve
Ventilation hose with flame arrester between rocker cover and throttle chamber
diagrams.mechanic_notes: White open arrows indicate fresh air intake; solid black arrows indicate blow-by gas flow through internal engine passages.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-23 Checking evaporative emission control system
diagrams.description: Test setup schematic for evaporative vapor line pressure leak check using 3-way cock, compressed air source, manometer, and connections to vapor-liquid separator and carbon canister.
measurements_and_specs: Allowable drop after 2.5 minutes: within 25 mmH2O (0.98 inH2O)
wiring_and_connections: Vapor line between carbon canister and vapor-liquid separator
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Removing filler cap should cause manometer reading to drop quickly to zero; failure to drop indicates clogged vent line.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-24 Replacing carbon canister filter
diagrams.description: Removal and replacement of bottom filter element from charcoal carbon canister body.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check for saturated or contaminated filter element and replace periodically.

diagrams.caption: Fig. ET-25 Fuel filler cap
diagrams.description: Sectional view of fuel tank filler cap showing internal vacuum relief valve and spring mechanism.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Clean housing and test by inhaling; slight initial resistance should be felt followed by audible valve clicking and opening.

diagrams.caption: ST10640001 Pivot adjuster
diagrams.description: Special service tool ST10640001 (Kent-Moore J 25615-01) curved pivot adjuster offset wrench used for valve lash adjustment on L-series OHC engines.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Enables loosening and tightening of rocker pivot lock nut while adjusting pivot screw.

diagrams.caption: ST19320000 Oil filter wrench
diagrams.description: Special service tool ST19320000 (Kent-Moore J 25664) band-type oil filter removal wrench.
components: ST19320000 Oil filter wrench band and handle
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use only for filter removal; replacement oil filter should be hand tightened.

Noisy engine (Mechanical knocking - Crankshaft bearing knocking)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Strong dull noise increases when engine is accelerated; stops by misfire on defective cylinder. Caused by worn or damaged bearings, or unevenly worn crankshaft.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Renew bearings and adjust or change crankshaft. Check lubrication system.

troubleshooting.symptom: Noisy engine (Mechanical knocking - Connecting rod bearing knocking)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Higher-pitched noise than crankshaft knocking, increases when engine accelerated; diminishes almost completely on misfire of defective cylinder.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Same as the case of crankshaft bearings.

troubleshooting.symptom: Noisy engine (Mechanical knocking - Piston and cylinder noise)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Overlapping metallic noise which increases with engine revolution and decreases as engine warms up; caused by piston and cylinder.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: This may cause an abnormal wearing of cylinder and lower compression which in turn will cause a lower out-put power and excessive consumption of oil. Overhaul engine.

troubleshooting.symptom: Noisy engine (Mechanical knocking - Piston pin noise)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Noise heard at each highest and lowest dead end of piston; locate by causing misfire on each cylinder.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: This may cause a wear on piston pin, or piston pin hole. Renew piston and piston pin assembly.

troubleshooting.symptom: Noisy engine (Mechanical knocking - Water pump noise)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Worn or damaged bearings, or uneven surface of sliding parts in water pump.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace water pump with a new one.

troubleshooting.symptom: Noisy engine (Others)
